rationale: This sample is a tiny Shootout-style C++ binary (481 bytes of text, only 3 functions) whose code is dominated by a single hot numeric loop in main (random number generation), so the weight table favors cheap, low-risk arithmetic-level obfuscation and penalizes loop-destabilizing passes: SUB gets the highest weights because random.cpp is arithmetic-heavy and SUB adds strong expression-level diversity with negligible runtime/size cost and near-zero correctness risk, while SPLIT is kept moderately high since it costs almost nothing and enlarges the block pool that makes SUB/IBR more effective; BCF and FLA receive low RuntimeCost weights because opaque predicates and control-flow flattening on the single hot inner loop would cause a disproportionate slowdown for a benchmark-shaped workload, and only moderate security weights since there is little multi-path control flow to hide in a 404-byte main; IBR sits in the middle as a usable runtime-tolerable diversifier of branch structure; and ICALL/IGV are weighted low because with 3 functions and virtually no indirect-call sites or global-variable surface in this sample there is little to transform, making their overhead-bearing application unjustified.
